text: Receipts show the files staging actually used (#400, #410). Python application receipts count and hash every staged regular file under each existing selection, bin/ and out/ included, in the same path-and-length digest. Before, they hashed with HashExisting's directory exclusions and showed fewer files than ran. Go, standalone TypeScript and existing-package TypeScript reports record file_selection, git or directory, for the root each actually staged. Markdown explains it, the fingerprint binds it, and model-only and older reports carry none. A root its repository ignores falls back to the whole directory when all its tracked ordinary files are deleted from the work tree, not only when nothing is tracked, so a Go build no longer stages an empty module. A surviving tracked entry, or a root the repository doesn't ignore, keeps Git selection. An explicit selection still can't step into a nested repository, the gap the build's first review found. Git failures, submodules and strict Python application staging still refuse.
